sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Jefferson County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Three offices share the job. The Assessor values the property, the County Clerk runs the first appeal board, and the Collector sends the bill and takes the payment. All three work from the Administration Center at 729 Maple Street in Hillsboro, the county seat.

  • Assessor, real estate questions: 636-797-5343. Personal property: 636-797-5466. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.
  • County Clerk, Board of Equalization appointments: 636-797-5478.
  • Collector, bills and payments: 636-797-5406, mailing address P.O. Box 100, Hillsboro, MO 63050.

Rates come from the school, fire, ambulance and other districts that cover your parcel, not from the Assessor or Collector. A house in Fox C-6 and a house in Hillsboro R-3 can carry quite different totals for that reason.

sections.h2: What does the Jefferson County housing picture look like for sellers?
sections.html:
Jefferson County sits on the Mississippi River south of St. Louis and covers about 657 square miles of land. Arnold is the largest city, Hillsboro is the seat, and Festus, De Soto, Crystal City, Herculaneum and Pevely fill out the list of incorporated places. The county is part of the St. Louis metropolitan area, and in 1980 it held the mean center of U.S. population (Wikipedia).

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page counts 233,132 residents as of July 2025 and 96,228 housing units. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $237,200 for 2020 to 2024, and 82.2% of households own. Median household income is $82,851 and the mean travel time to work is 30.6 minutes.

With more than four in five households owning, a large share of tax bills here are paid by lenders from escrow, which makes the lender request rule in the due-date section below worth knowing.

sections.h2: How does the Jefferson County Assessor value a home?
sections.html:
The Assessor uses mass appraisal. Replacement cost of the buildings is reduced for depreciation, then land value is added to reach fair market value (Assessor FAQ). Missouri requires every parcel to be reassessed in odd-numbered years, and 2027 is the next one.

Market value is then multiplied by the assessment level for the property class. A $100,000 house is carried at $19,000 of assessed value.

Assessment levels used in Jefferson County (Assessor FAQ)
Property classShare of market value taxed
Residential19%
Commercial32%
Agricultural12%

Your bill can change without a reassessment. A new garage, an adjoining acre or a finished house that had been prorated during construction all move assessed value, and a voter-approved levy change moves the total even when value stays flat.

sections.h2: When is Jefferson County property tax due, and what happens if it is late?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due December 31 and becomes delinquent on January 1. Bills go on the county website in November and are mailed late that month. If nothing arrives by December 1, call the Collector, because a missing bill does not excuse the deadline.

  • Pay at 729 Maple Street, online, or by the phone line at 1-877-289-0099 (the Collector's FAQ lists a convenience fee of 2.5% with a $1.95 minimum for debit and cards, and $4.95 for e-check).
  • Mailed payments need a postmark of December 31 or earlier, so check the last pickup time at your post office.
  • Mortgage companies must send the Collector a written request for each bill they plan to pay. If you received a paper bill, your lender did not ask for it.

The Collector has no power to waive penalty or interest, citing section 139.100 and an Attorney General opinion. Under RSMo 140.100, land in the back tax book carries an 18 percent penalty on each year's delinquency, and the penalty on land redeemed before sale cannot exceed 2 percent per month.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Jefferson County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a phone call to the Assessor. An appraiser reviews the value with you and looks at any evidence you bring. If that does not settle it, you file with the Board of Equalization through the County Clerk. The county's assessor page and the State Tax Commission both give the second Monday in July as the filing cutoff. The 2026 date was July 13 and has passed, and the next one is July 12, 2027.

  1. Call the Assessor at 636-797-5343 and ask for an informal review.
  2. Call the County Clerk at 636-797-5478 for the forms and a hearing date.
  3. Bring five copies of any written evidence: one for each board member, one for the board secretary and one for the Assessor.
  4. Expect a certified letter with the decision, usually within 5 business days.
  5. If you still disagree, file a Complaint for Review of Assessment with the State Tax Commission, attaching the board's decision letter.

The county's collector page gives the State Tax Commission cutoff as September 30 or 30 days after the board decision, whichever is later. The Commission's own guide says the 30 days run from the date of the letter, and that a property owned by an LLC, trust, corporation or estate needs an attorney to file.

Taxes still have to be paid by December 31 while an appeal is open. Paying under protest follows a specific procedure: full payment before the delinquency date plus a written statement of your grounds and your claimed fair market value. Writing "protest" on the check does nothing on its own.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs apply to Jefferson County homeowners?
sections.html:
The county lists two. One is a Real Property Tax Credit for Seniors, enacted February 15, 2024, with details on the county's Assessor FAQ page. The other is the state's Property Tax Credit Claim, which returns part of the real estate tax or rent paid during the year.

  • The state credit is capped at $1,100 for owners who live in their home and $750 for renters.
  • You may qualify if you are 65 by December 31 of the prior year, or you or your spouse are 100% disabled, or you are 60 or older and receive surviving spouse benefits.
  • Household income, counting Social Security, cannot exceed $30,000 for a single person or $34,000 for married homeowners.
  • File with form MO-1040 and schedule MO-PTS, or form MO-PTC if you do not file an income tax return.

An owner whose house is destroyed by a tornado, flood, fire or earthquake can ask the Assessor to remove the residential value on a pro-rata basis under section 137.082, using the Destroyed Residential Property form.

sections.h2: How are taxes handled when a Jefferson County house sells?
sections.html:
The Collector's FAQ says that in most closings the seller's share of the year's tax is credited on the settlement statement and the buyer is responsible for the full year. Your settlement statement or title company shows the exact split.

Once the new deed is recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office, the Assessor's file shows the new owner. The name on a real estate bill changes only through a recorded deed, so the bill address and the owner name will not update from a phone call alone.

If a house you are selling has a delinquent year, ask the Collector for the amount due including penalty and interest before you accept an offer, and have the title company pay it from the proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to pay Jefferson County real estate tax?
faqs.a: December 31 of the tax year. Payments postmarked after that date are charged penalty and interest, and the Collector cannot waive either one.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Jefferson County value?
faqs.a: No for the county board. The second Monday in July was July 13, 2026, and has passed. Missouri reassesses in odd-numbered years, so 2027 brings new notices and a July 12, 2027 filing date.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Jefferson County tax bill never arrived?
faqs.a: Call the Collector at 636-797-5406. The county asks owners to call if nothing has arrived by December 1, and the deadline stays December 31 either way.

faqs.q: Does my mortgage lender pay the Jefferson County bill?
faqs.a: Only if it sent the Collector a written request for your bill. If the paper bill came to you, the lender did not request it, so call the lender to learn where it wants the bill sent.

faqs.q: Who pays the year's tax when I sell my Jefferson County house?
faqs.a: By the Collector's account, the seller's portion is usually credited at closing and the buyer owes the whole year's bill. Your settlement statement lays out the split.
